ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (as amended) (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 462.3-462.5; Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, Part 2 (individuals with significant control (ISC) register); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, as amended by Bill C-42 (federal beneficial ownership registry); Retail Payment Activities Act, SC 2021, c 23 (Bank of Canada registration and risk management regime for payment service providers); Special Economic Measures Act, RSC 1985, c S-8; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c 21.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin of each signatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by certified translation into English where necessary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary public of the foreign corporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance screening of all founders, directors, officers and beneficial owners against the consolidated Canadian sanctions list (Special Economic Measures Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act and United Nations Act lists administered by Global Affairs Canada and OSFI), OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists (required by correspondent US clearing banks for Visa/Mastercard and Fedwire settlement), and FINTRAC-mandated enhanced due diligence for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons and heads of international organizations (PCMLTFA s 9.3 and applicable FINTRAC guidance). Screening must be evidence-based, repeatable at each subsequent incorporation step, and escalated to senior management for approval where any positive or ambiguous match occurs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), accessible exclusively through designated Registry Agents and the official online platform at https://www.albertacorporateidentity.ca; federal alternative: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre at https://www.ic.gc.ca/corporate (NUANS name search and incorporation), followed by extra-provincial registration in Alberta if a federal corporation is used.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use the basic Latin alphabet (A-Z), Arabic numerals (0-9), and permitted punctuation (hyphens, periods, ampersands). Diacritical marks are not used in NUANS-indexed names in Alberta. Where a non-English word or brand is used, a standard Latin-script transliteration must be submitted, and the name must be pronounceable, distinctive, and free of prohibited connotations. French-language or bilingual forms are permissible under the federal Corporations Canada regime.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANK, BANKING, TRUST, TRUSTEE, LOAN, FINANCIAL (requires evidence of a chartered bank, trust company, or authorized financial-services licence)
CANADA (requires written consent where the name suggests government sponsorship)
ALBERTA (geographically suggestive; requires consent or demonstrated distinctiveness)
UNIVERSITY, COLLEGE, INSTITUTE (triggers post-secondary education licensing consent)
ENGINEER, ENGINEERING (restricted under Alberta's Engineering and Geoscience Professions Act)
ROYAL, CROWN, MUNICIPAL, CO-OPERATIVE (restricted tokens implying public or special constitution)
VISA, MASTERCARD (trade-marked network tokens; refused unless written membership or authorization evidence is provided)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name reservation may be reconsidered by filing a written Request for Review with the Director of Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) within 30 days of the rejection, attaching the NUANS report, the requested name, a legal memorandum on distinctiveness, and any written consents from holders of conflicting names. If the Director upholds the refusal, the applicant may refile a revised NUANS search, apply for a fresh 90-day reservation, or commence judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta. Extension of an existing reservation is available for a further 90-day period upon demonstration of good-faith exigent circumstances, and must be filed before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only in the limited sense that an Alberta-licensed corporate service provider may act as registered office at its physical address. However, a high-risk PSP engaged in online merchant acquiring and clearing must, as a FINTRAC-registered money services business and a payment service provider under the Retail Payment Activities Act, maintain a real physical place of business in Canada where books, records, AML/CFT compliance files, and client identification records are kept and made available for examination. A virtual mailbox or shell address is not acceptable as the operational seat for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: estimated 75% probability of a FINTRAC compliance examination or Bank of Canada supervisory inspection within the first three years of operation for a cross-border payment-gateway PSP clearing US card rails and Fedwire; unannounced on-site examinations are authorized under the PCMLTFA compliance framework.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, ss. 9, 12, 13, 16, 21, 101, 102, 110; Corporate Registry Regulation, Alta Reg 183/2001.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, 100-10405 Jasper Avenue, Edmonton, AB T5J 4B7, Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1), Notice of Registered Office (Form 2), and Notice of Directors (Form 3)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; no escrow account is mandatory for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation adopts its Articles of Incorporation filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry, and the Corporation shall have perpetual succession; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the purchase and issuance of 100 common shares to the initial subscriber for stated consideration is approved; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [address], Alberta, Canada; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [name] and [name] are appointed as directors for the first term ending at the first annual general meeting; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed President and [name] is appointed Corporate Secretary; AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that officers are authorized to open corporate bank accounts, execute regulatory filings, and secure all operating and financial services licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Approval and Corporate Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta — Alberta Corporate Registration System (ACRS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS pre-screening through ACRS or an authorized service provider. Submit a corporate name reservation request identifying the proposed name, examination report reference, and corporate legal elements. If the name is distinct, the Registry reserves it for up to 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to actual confusion, submit an alternate name list within the reservation period. If the refusal is based on an administrative error, file a written complaint with the Registrar of Corporations seeking expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (ACRS online filing portal or Edmonton registry office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Articles of Incorporation specifying the authorized share structure, share classes, rights and restrictions, number of directors, and first directors. Attach the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors. Verify all signatures satisfy Alberta statutory declaration requirements. Pay the incorporation fee and submit through ACRS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporate Registry issues a query or deficiency notice, file a corrected or amended document within the stated cure period, normally 14 business days. If registration is rejected, refile with full corrections; the Registry's decision may be appealed under the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon compliance review by Corporate Registry, the Registrar executes and issues a Certificate of Incorporation. The corporate existence begins on the certificate date. The certificate should be retrieved electronically or in paper form and maintained in the corporate records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond SLA, request expedited processing by contacting the Registrar. If the certificate contains a typographical error, submit a corrected certificate application or Articles of Amendment to rectify the record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Meeting and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or adopt resolutions by written consent. Approve corporate bylaws, appoint officers, accept subscribers' share subscriptions, issue share certificates, and adopt a share register, minute book, and corporate seal if required. Record the first registered office and directors in the corporate records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board resolution is later found defective, directors may ratify and cure the action through a unanimous supplemental resolution. If ministerial steps were improperly taken, re-execute the relevant corporate instrument with board approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Corporate Return and Federal Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online and Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Alberta initial corporate return with the Registry and register for a federal Business Number (BN) with the CRA. Request applicable program accounts, including GST/HST, import/export, and payroll where relevant. Provide certificate details and registered office information, and confirm the registered office and directors are updated in the Alberta registry.
required_dossiers: Corporate registered office and director information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or queries the registration, correct and resubmit through the Business Registration Online portal within 30 days. If the Alberta initial return is flagged, respond to the Registry's notice by filing the missing or corrected information.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for federal money services business registration; Service Alberta for provincial consumer business licensing and municipal business licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Money Services Business (MSB) Registration under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); Alberta Consumer Services business licence where required by municipal regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas and Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required — the business is a non-manufacturing financial services and administrative headquarters operation with no effluent discharge, air emissions, or hazardous waste generation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial wastewater or VOCs. Electronic waste management must follow Alberta Recycling Regulation and ECCC storage guidelines for computer hardware; no physical process discharges are generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code compliance certificate under the OHS Act for the registered premises; commercial building fire safety inspection verifying compliance with the Alberta Fire Code and National Fire Code; structural load clearance for leased office equipment; municipal occupancy permit obtained from the local land-use authority.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in coordination with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for foreign exchange and cross-border payment oversight
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free-floating exchange currency with no exchange control legislation. Current account convertibility is fully unrestricted. Capital account transactions are equally unrestricted, except that large direct or indirect acquisitions fall under the Investment Canada Act (ICA) review thresholds. Profit remittances by way of dividends, interest, royalties, or management fees are lawful without pre-approval from the Bank of Canada; such payments are subject to Part XIII Canadian withholding tax, potentially reduced by applicable tax treaties. Corporate treasury flows require no conversion permit, but all cross-border EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC and are subject to bank-enhanced due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None under Canadian law. Canada does not impose currency surrender requirements, mandatory conversion ratios, or prescribed timelines for export receipts. Exporters may legitimately retain foreign-currency proceeds in Canadian or foreign bank accounts, convert at market rates at a time of their choosing, or use those balances for hedge or treasury operations. All such transactions remain subject to standard anti-money laundering recordkeeping and FINTRAC reporting thresholds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a supplemental treasury corridor only; low as a primary banking rail. Canada does not recognize a foreign electronic money institution (EMI) license as equivalent to a Canadian depository license. Offshore digital EMI accounts cannot be used to provide CAD settlement services to Canadian clients or access Payment Canada clearing rails unless the EMI is separately registered as a Canadian money services business (MSB) under the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC. An MSB-registered foreign EMI may hold settlement floats, but OSFI and the chartered banks will generally classify the EMI as higher-risk and demand full penetration testing, compliance audit rights, and transparency on merchant counterparties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a PSP classified as high risk under ISIC 6619, Canadian Tier 1 banks normally require in-person or secure live video attendance of the founder, compliance officer, and majority of directors before opening the account. Remote corporate onboarding is accepted only for directors who are resident in Canada or in FATF-equivalent jurisdictions and can pass enhanced due diligence with notarized corporate documents, banking references, and audited compliance programs. Physical presence is effectively mandatory for non-resident directors, particularly where the entity is newly incorporated and has no operating history inside Canada.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business sector: cross-border merchant acquiring and payment facilitation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC money services business (MSB) registration certificate; provincial/city business license; comprehensive written AML/ATF program; independent compliance audit report; documented transaction monitoring system; customer and merchant risk classification matrix; board-approved AML policy; recent regulatory correspondence and no-actions letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque group structure with non-resident parent or offshore holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organizational chart showing all intermediate entities and natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; certified registry extracts for every entity; notarized shareholder register and share transfer records; declarations of source of wealth and source of funds; statutory declarations of direct and indirect control; independent legal opinion confirming the natural-person UBO recognition; consent letters for enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions scraping or adverse media hit on a settlement counterparty or downstream merchant
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions screening logs covering OFAC, UN, EU, and OSFI lists; negative news search archive with timestamps; residual risk assessment completed by the compliance officer; documented mitigation program for true-name matches; terminated merchant or counterparty exposure reports; audit trail of enhanced monitoring implementation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained or non-transparent source of initial capital injection into the escrow/operating account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source bank statement of the remitting and parent company; wire originator and beneficiary details; executed share subscription agreement; notarized board resolution authorizing the capital injection; certified tax clearance certificate; notarized loan or deed-of-gift instrument where applicable; sworn declaration from the ultimate director detailing the transaction chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is via SWIFT MT103 through the final Canadian beneficiary bank, with full FATF Travel Rule originator and beneficiary information, including the payer legal name, address, regulatory identifier (where available), the receiving corporation's name, Canadian Business Number (BN), registered address, and account number. The payment narrative or purpose field must clearly read 'Capital Subscription - Share Purchase' or 'Paid-in Capital Contribution'. The receiving bank will require the corporate certificate of incorporation, shareholder resolution approving the capital injection, proof of source of funds, and may require a FINTRAC EFT report for transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. No Bank of Canada permit is required; foreign takeover review under the Investment Canada Act applies only where the transaction exceeds the applicable enterprise value limits. The inbound payment will be settled into the CAD operating account through Lynx or the bank's internal ledgers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 via Canadian correspondent banking for all foreign currency settlements. Documentary trade obligations are cleared through commercial letters of credit issued or advised under UCP 600 using MT700/MT707 SWIFT messages, with drafts and documents negotiated through the Canadian bank. For high-value domestic CAD clearing, use Lynx (formerly LVTS); for instant small-value payments use Payment Canada's Real-Time Rail. Merchant and card clearing for the payment gateway itself settles via Visa Base II and Mastercard MIP; the net settlement position is credited or debited to the PSP's settlement account at the Tier 1 bank. For jurisdictions with restricted conversion markets, treasury must pre-negotiate USD or EUR corridor accounts to avoid reliance on local emerging-market clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or less-liquid currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD $100 late filing fee; failure to file for 2 consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off/dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Alberta Corporate Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (up to 12%); 10% penalty for repeat failure; failure to file may lead to statute-barred assessments

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not compulsory for private (non-offering) Alberta corporations if shareholders unanimously waive an auditor each fiscal year; a compulsory audit exists for offering corporations or when payment gateway licensing regulations mandate independent audits
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (public enterprises under Canada's accounting framework); ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO filing to the Alberta Corporate Registry; maintain an internal separate register of individuals with significant control (ISC) and update within 15 days of a change; the annual return does not require UBO disclosure
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general (15% federal + 8% Alberta); 11% on first C$500,000 active business income of qualifying CCPCs (9% federal + 2% Alberta)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC small business deduction; SR&ED investment tax credits up to 35% refundable for CCPCs; Accelerated Investment Incentive first-year CCA; Alberta Investor Tax Credit 30%; no Alberta capital tax
